workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks in order 1 (daemon pane identity) → 2 (provisioning one-time unset) → 3 (extension stops writing config) → 4 (docs) → 5 (push, PR); TDD per task — write the named test, watch the named failure, implement, watch it pass — one `jj split` commit per task with only the named paths, one pull request. Tasks 1–3 are independent in code, but Task 2 also edits processes.test.ts (the exact provisioning command list), so keep the order. Tester: criterion 3 on two real workspaces of the provisioned clone (no-trace recipe in the plan), criterion 1 on a real worker pane via /proc/<pane_pid>/environ, negative controls named. Reviewer: every acceptance row against the plan inventory table; the six-variable contract against the diff.

implement: legion-worker — shared workspace binding, jj-only commits via `jj split`, bookmark legion/LEGION-44, PR body in READY format with `Dispatch: LEGION-44`.
test-driven-development — each task writes its test first and watches the exact failure named in the plan before implementing.
verification-before-completion — three package suites green locally (packages/workspace has no CI job; its `bun test` summary goes in the PR body).
test: legion-worker — criterion 3 is tester evidence on two real workspaces of the provisioned clone (plan section `Tester`), quoting author/committer from `jj log`; criterion 1 on a real spawned worker pane's environ with the controller pane as negative control; no permanent test for criterion 3 by spec.
review: legion-worker — verify CI/Threads/E2E against GitHub; check the acceptance→test inventory table; confirm root/controller panes carry none of the six variables and that no `jj config set` call site remains anywhere (grep in Task 5 Step 1).

concerns: packages/workspace has no CI job (pr-and-main.yaml runs packages/daemon only; envoy-and-contracts.yaml never lists it): Task 2 tests are gated by the implementer/tester local runs recorded in the PR body. LEGION-70 planned to add the job; check .github/workflows at implementation time.

Out of scope, observed: catchup.ts MODE_TO_ROLE maps planner/tester/architect catch-up reads to the review App while appRoleForLegionRole (identity+credentials, used here per spec) maps them to implement — pre-existing inconsistency in a read-only path.

Out of scope, observed: workspace.ts:204-213 recovery path runs `jj workspace forget <name> --cleanup --force`; neither jj 0.45.1 (fork) nor stock 0.44.0 on this box accepts --cleanup/--force (`jj workspace forget --help` lists neither) — that branch would fail with an argument error if ever reached.

Out of scope, observed: scripts/smoke/checkpoints.sh:303 asserts `implementer+ses_` identity and a `Legion-Session:` trailer, and :346-348 asserts the reviewer App authored the .legion deletion — all predate the current design (App-identity emails, `Omp-Session` trailer, implementer pushes the deletion).

Tests that seed a repo-scoped key on real jj (Task 2 Step 4, Task 3 Step 1) leave an empty ~/.config/jj/repos/<hash>/config.toml for the temp repo behind — both jj builds store repo config there; same footprint as the test being replaced.
verifiedFacts: `jj config path --repo` for a workspace and for its clone print the same file (~/.config/jj/repos/<hash>/config.toml) on jj 0.45.1-sami and stock 0.44.0 — the shared file the spec describes.

`jj config list --repo -R <dir> user.name`: exit 0; `user.name = "X"` when set, empty stdout + stderr warning when unset. `jj config unset --repo -R <dir> user.name`: exit 0 when set; exit 1 `Error: "user.name" doesn't exist` when unset. Both builds.

With repo config user.name set, `JJ_USER=Env JJ_EMAIL=e jj new` yields author and committer `Env <e>`; with only GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* set, jj keeps the repo-config identity — both variable sets are needed.

`jj workspace add` under JJ_USER/JJ_EMAIL creates the workspace's working-copy commit with that author+committer; `jj describe` under an identity refreshes the committer; `jj workspace forget` abandons an empty undescribed working-copy commit but keeps a described one as a visible head — basis of the tester's no-trace recipe.

processes.test.ts:7153 asserts the worker pane env with toEqual (gains the six keys); :825 asserts controller+root env with toEqual (standing negative control); :684 asserts the exact provisioning command list (gains the two probes). No test's tokenManager.getToken rejects on a spawn path.

legion.ts:478 `const workspace = requiredEnvironment(process.env, "LEGION_WORKSPACE")` has exactly one reader, the setJjIdentity call at :512; nothing else in packages/pi-envoy reads LEGION_WORKSPACE.
